requirements.requirement: Treat /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 as the authoritative source and maintain a synchronized copy on node2.
requirements.summary: The synchronization is unidirectional from node1 to a restricted atomic receiver on node2. Initial and subsequent observations show identical file hashes and contents on both nodes, including after both nodes restarted.

requirements.requirement: Automatically propagate changes from node1 to node2 within 15 minutes.
requirements.summary: A path watcher and persistent five-minute fallback timer were enabled. A live source change reached node2 with matching content in about 9 seconds. After bounded sequential restarts, another source change reached node2 in about 7 seconds, directly demonstrating recovered automatic synchronization well inside 15 minutes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 is the demonstrated source for a durable, restricted node1-to-node2 synchronization mechanism, and two observed changes propagated in seconds, including after successful restarts of both managed nodes. Restart evidence and lifecycle cross-checks are complete and coherent, with no operational-hygiene defects identified.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the chronological command trace. File, credential, receiver, and systemd changes directly implemented the synchronization outcome; test edits were bounded functional evidence; restarts and related service starts established the mandatory restart evidence and recovered state. No unwanted residue is observed: both nodes have no failed services, package health remains good, listening endpoints are unchanged apart from post-reboot process IDs, and temporary-file differences are ordinary reboot-generated systemd directories. The restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and recovered services and synchronized data.
